instruction: Freeze the top 4 rows so the header row stays visible while scrolling down.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully zoomed out the spreadsheet from 260% to 100% by navigating View > Zoom menu in LibreOffice Calc. Completed in 4 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc View menu, access Zoom submenu, change zoom level
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different View menu feature (freeze rows) using the same spreadsheet. Model demonstrated ability to navigate View menu; now tests freeze pane functionality which is also under View menu.
metadata.explanation: Getter reads freeze_panes property from xlsx. Metric checks if freeze is set to A5 (rows 1-4 frozen). Header row is at row 4, so freezing top 4 rows means data starts scrolling from row 5. Postconfig saves file before evaluation.

scoring_breakdown.freeze_correct: 1.0 - Freeze panes set to A5 (top 4 rows frozen)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts freeze_panes property from the xlsx file using openpyxl, which is the right state for verifying row freezing.
Expected value 'A5' is semantically correct: freezing at A5 means rows 1-4 are frozen, matching the instruction to freeze top 4 rows.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' — accesses expected.get('expected_freeze') directly without wrapping in 'rules'.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation, ensuring the freeze pane state is persisted to disk.
Complete coverage: the single instruction requirement (freeze top 4 rows) is fully verified by checking freeze_panes == 'A5'.
